articles.title: Free mint on Base: what the buyer pays and what the creator stores
articles.excerpt: What a buyer actually pays on a free mint: gas only, with the real number on Base and how it compares to buying the same token on the secondary market My mint function takes no payment. The buyer pays…
articles.body: What a buyer actually pays on a free mint: gas only, with the real number on Base and how it compares to buying the same token on the secondary market My mint function takes no payment. The buyer pays only the Base transaction gas required to execute the mint. There is no honest fixed ETH number for that gas cost. Base fees change with network conditions, and the final amount also depends on the contract execution path. The real number is the wallet’s gas estimate multiplied by the current gas price when the transaction is submitted. I check it immediately before minting: const request = { account : buyer , address : contractAddress , abi , functionName : " mint " , }; const gas = await publicClient . estimateContractGas ( request ); const gasPrice = await publicClient .

articles.excerpt: When Machines Fail, Experience Shouldn't Be Forgotten: The Story Behind RecallOps By Vasundhara S | Hack with Bangalore 4.0 A Problem That Made Me Think Differently Imagine working in a factory where…
articles.body: When Machines Fail, Experience Shouldn't Be Forgotten: The Story Behind RecallOps By Vasundhara S | Hack with Bangalore 4.0 A Problem That Made Me Think Differently Imagine working in a factory where hundreds of machines operate every day. One morning, an important machine suddenly stops working. The maintenance team spends hours inspecting components, identifying possible causes, and trying different repairs. Eventually, they solve the problem. But what happens to everything they learned during those hours? The successful repair might be recorded somewhere. The unsuccessful attempts might be forgotten. And when another machine develops a similar problem, a different technician could end up repeating the same troubleshooting process. This made me think about something important.

articles.title: How to explain a crypto product on video without sounding like a pitch
articles.excerpt: Crypto and web3 products have a trust problem before they have a feature problem. The viewer has seen the rocket emojis and the "100x" claims, so the first question is not "what does it do?" but "is t…
articles.body: Crypto and web3 products have a trust problem before they have a feature problem. The viewer has seen the rocket emojis and the "100x" claims, so the first question is not "what does it do?" but "is this a scam?" A product video that ignores that question loses people in the first ten seconds. Here is how I plan these videos when a wallet, protocol or exchange team asks me to animate something. Start by lowering the viewer's guard Skip the hype opener. Open on the specific job the product does for a specific person: "move funds between chains without three separate apps" or "see exactly what a contract will do before you sign it." A plain, checkable sentence signals that nothing here depends on excitement. Show the flow, not the vision People trust what they can follow.

articles.body: Stop shipping multi-megabyte desktop databases to the browser—the Web finally has its own DB. At that point, you have two choices—and both hurt. Option 1: The IndexedDB Boilerplate Trap You start with raw IndexedDB (or a thin wrapper around it). articles.title: Why Your Next IDE Might Actually Be a Git Client
articles.excerpt: A few weeks ago I wrote about why I left GitKraken and built Gitoryx. That post was about the tool I left behind. This one is about something I noticed while building the replacement: the more I used…
articles.body: A few weeks ago I wrote about why I left GitKraken and built Gitoryx . That post was about the tool I left behind. This one is about something I noticed while building the replacement: the more I used Gitoryx day to day, the less I opened my IDE for anything other than editing code. That's not a small shift. For years, the IDE was the center of gravity. Everything else, the terminal, the Git GUI, the AI assistant, orbited around it as a separate window you alt-tabbed into. I didn't plan to change that. It just stopped making sense once the pieces lived in one place. Key Takeaways Keeping the terminal inside the same app as your Git client removes a whole category of alt-tabbing and lost context, especially when you're watching an AI make changes in real time.

articles.title: Northern lights could reach New York and Idaho this weekend as speedy solar wind races toward Earth
articles.excerpt: A colossal coronal hole on the sun is unleashing a stream of high-speed solar wind that could spark impressive auroras Nov. 6-8.
articles.body: The northern lights could put on an impressive display this weekend as a colossal coronal hole on the sun fires a stream of high-speed solar wind toward Earth. Minor (G1) geomagnetic storm conditions between Nov. 6 and Nov. 8, with a chance of moderate (G2) conditions on Nov. 7 and Nov. 8, according to NOAA's Space Weather Prediction Center (SWPC) . If G2 conditions materialize, the northern lights could be visible as far south as New York and Idaho. What is happening? The culprit behind the potential uptick in northern lights is a large coronal hole on the sun , a region where the sun's magnetic field opens up. They allow streams of charged particles known as the solar wind to escape more easily into space.

articles.body: When Like a Dragon Gaiden: The Man Who Erased His Name was released in 2023, the Yakuza series was in a strange position. The team at Sega's Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio was gearing up to give a heroic sendoff to longtime protagonist Kazuma Kiryu. They had big plans for 2024's Like a Dragon: Infinite Wealth to pass the torch to a new main character. But Yakuza had unexpectedly become bigger than ever outside Japan, thanks largely to the viral success of Yakuza 0 throughout the late 2010s and early 2020s. The fans demanded more Kiryu, not less. And developer Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio rose to the occasion with The Man Who Erased His Name , an interquel that depicts his lonely years in exile after the events of Yakuza 6.

articles.title: 4-billion-year-old 'Rosetta Stone' found in Sahara Desert could unlock the secret history of water on Mars
articles.excerpt: A rock discovered in the Sahara Desert formed more than 4.1 billion years ago, making it one of the oldest Martian meteorites ever found. The ancient space rock offers a rare glimpse into the formatio…
articles.body: A rose-colored rock discovered in the Sahara Desert may hold some clues to Mars' ancient geological history. The meteorite , named Teghaza 001 after the salt plain in Mali where it was discovered in 2022, weighs roughly 1.8 pounds (800 grams) and formed more than 4.1 billion years ago. Blasted off Mars by an impact before eventually landing on Earth, it is one of the three oldest Martian meteorites ever found. The extraordinary age and unusual mineral composition of Teghaza 001 offer a rare glimpse into the formation of Mars' early crust and how volcanic materials may have been altered by water, according to a statement from NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory in Southern California.

Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. A Farewell to Swift Explanation: It is time to say goodbye to NASA ‘s Neil Gehrels Swift Observatory . After nearly 22 years of service, the satellite re-entered Earth’s atmosphere on November 4 at 7:39 EST over the North Sumatra region of Indonesia . The featured image is a mosaic created in 2018 using the first one million images captured by the satellite’s Ultraviolet/Optical Telescope .
